question: How Do I Add a Shipment Tracking Number to an Order?
metaDescription: Not built into WooCommerce core — a dedicated shipment tracking plugin adds the field and automatically includes it in customer notification emails.
shortAnswer: WooCommerce core doesn't include a tracking number field by default — this needs a dedicated shipment tracking plugin (several free and premium options exist), which adds a tracking number and carrier field to each order, automatically includes a tracking link in the customer's shipping notification email, and often supports bulk tracking entry for stores processing many shipments at once.

bodyHtml:
Why This Needs a Plugin

Shipment tracking is inherently tied to whichever carrier or fulfillment method a specific store uses, and WooCommerce core deliberately stays carrier-agnostic rather than building in support for any specific tracking system. A dedicated tracking plugin fills this gap, typically supporting a wide range of common carriers with pre-built tracking URL formats, plus the ability to add a custom carrier if needed.

What to Look For in a Tracking Plugin

  • Automatic inclusion in the shipping/completed order email, so customers get the tracking link without any extra manual step beyond entering it on the order.
  • Support for the specific carriers actually used by the store, or an easy way to add a custom carrier with its own tracking URL format if using a less common one.
  • Bulk entry support if the store processes many shipments daily, since entering tracking numbers one order at a time doesn't scale well for higher-volume stores.
  • Customer-facing tracking display in My Account order history, letting customers check status without needing to search back through email.
  • Integration with a fulfillment or shipping label service, if one is in use, which can sometimes auto-populate tracking numbers directly rather than requiring manual entry at all.

Setting This Up

  1. Choose a shipment tracking plugin matching the store's carriers and volume needs.
  2. Confirm tracking links appear correctly in customer emails and My Account after adding a test tracking number.
  3. Consider a fulfillment integration that can auto-populate tracking if manual entry becomes a bottleneck at higher order volumes.

Need shipment tracking integrated with your specific fulfillment process? See custom WooCommerce development.
